title: Attention funnelizer + requant scheduling + continuous-batcher for improved quantized kernel throughput
author: Lena Park
description:
Motivation: Improve end-to-end throughput and p99 tail latency for INT8/FP8 inference paths without regressing quality. We observed that dequant->transpose->attention kernels were paying repeated per-token memory operations and poor packing across micro-batches, especially for short sequence workloads. This PR introduces an "attention funnelizer" kernel stage that fuses the dequant/scale step with q/k/v layout transforms and a small prefetch path, plus a lightweight requant scheduling layer that informs the runtime how to group micro-batches for vectorized microkernel execution. The continuous-batcher improvements ensure the runtime can maintain tight SLOs while enabling larger, opportunistic coalescing for throughput.

Changes in this PR: single-string description with checklist and notes: - implement AttnFunnelizer microkernel: fuse dequant+multiply-by-scale + q/k/v transpose + optional per-head requant hint. - add RequantScheduler policy hook to the continuous batching pipeline to produce aligned microbatch windows for INT8/FP8 kernels. - KV cache alignment changes to maintain zero-copy when AttnFunnelizer is used and ensure cache offsets remain 64-byte aligned across versions. - runtime config: new kernel_hint.attn_funnelizer.enabled and kernel_hint.requant.pack_size tunables exposed to Redwood Console. - tests and perf harness updates: microbench driver, integration perf test for 8x short-seq workloads. - docs: brief runtime/ops note and FAQ entry.

Why this is different: existing dequant fusion efforts focused on per-layer fusion; this work targets the attention path specifically and the interaction with continuous batching. Instead of collapsing many ops inside the backward-compatible attention kernel, the funnelizer produces a packed attention-ready buffer which downstream kernels can consume with minimal memory traffic and predictable alignment. The requant scheduling layer is runtime-only and does not change model exports.

Benchmarks (internal perf harness, A100, FP16 baseline vs INT8/FP8 variants): - INT8 + AttnFunnelizer + RequantScheduler: +18% median throughput, +12% 95th percentile throughput; p99 latency reduced by 8% in continuous-batching mode for short sequences (<=64). - FP8 with funnelizer: +10% throughput vs previous FP8 path, p99 -5%. - Memory traffic on the attention hotpath reduced ~22% measured by nvprof counters.

Compatibility and rollout: non-breaking for models that do not enable the kernel_hint flags. Default is off for public hosted rollout; enabled for dedicated clusters behind a feature flag. Provides safe fallback to the legacy dequant path if the kernel is not available or alignment constraints fail.

Checklist: - [x] Kernel microbench and functional tests - [x] Integration perf harness updates - [x] CI passing (flake run after addressing a clang-tidy complaint) - [x] Console config & docs - [x] Release notes entry

Notes and follow-ups: - Follow-up PR to add a lightweight auto-tuner that chooses pack_size based on observed sequence distribution (linked ENG-2114). - Investigate combining with per-head requant multipliers upstream in the model loader (design doc sketch linked).
